The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident took place on 11.10.2021.
2.

The brief contents of the petition are as under:
On 11.10.2021, at about 10.55 a.m., the petitioner was riding his Two Wheeler Dio bearing Reg. No.KA02 JE0132 near Nirmala Medicals, Vijayanandanagar SCCH-10 Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the TATA 709 EX Mini Lorry bearing Reg.No.EX 53AA1234 came on the same road with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle from back side.
Due to the impact, the petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
3. Further the petitioner submitted that, immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Confident Hospital, Shankarnagar, Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient.
After taking treatment, he was advised by the doctor to take rest and regular followup treatment.
Again petitioner was admitted on 12.12.2021 and he took treatment for two days.
The petitioner has contended that, he has spent Rs.2,50,000/ towards medicines, conveyance, food, nourishment and other incidental charges.

4. Further the petitioner stated that, prior to the SCCH-10 accident, he was hale and healthy, aged about 38 years, working as Writer cum Clerk in Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Traders,
Yeshwanthapura RMC Yard, Bengaluru and was getting a salary of Rs.30,000/p.m.
The alleged accident was occurred due to negligence on the part of the driver of the Tata 709 EX Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No.EX53AA1234.

The respondent No.1 being insurer and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Ramesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38174397/
2 petitioner.

sentences.text: Hence, on all these grounds, the petitioner prayed to allow this petition and award compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ under all heads together with interest and costs.
5. In response to the Court notice, the respondent No.1 made its appearance before the Court through its counsel and filed written statement, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
On the other hand, the respondent No.2 has not appeared before the Court, remained absent and placed exparte.
SCCH-10 6.
The brief contentions of the respondent No.1 are as under:
The respondent No.2 contended that, the petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts of the case and also denied the entire petition averments in toto.

Further submitted that, the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary and proper parties for the adjudication of the petition and further submits that the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA02JE 0132 without wearing helmet and without a valid and effective driving license ride the same on the date of accident.
Further this respondent has denied the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Tata 709 EX Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA53AA1234 and involvement of the same in the alleged accident.
Further it has admitted for the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and in favour of the respondent No.2.
However, the liability of this respondent is subjected to terms and conditions of the policy.

Further SCCH-10 contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not possess a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and seeks protection u/s 147 and 149 of M.V. Act.
7.
It is the allegation of the respondent No.1 that neither the owner nor jurisdictional police complied the mandatory provisions as required u/s 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It is the specific contention of this respondent that, the petitioner himself solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.

Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition against it.

8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 11.10.2021 at about 10.55 a.m., while the petitioner was proceeding on his Two Wheeler Dio bearing Reg. No.KA02JE0132 and when he reached near Nirmala Medicals, Vijayanagar SCCH-10 Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Tata 709 Ex Mini Lorry bearing No.KA53AA1234 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with a high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle from behind, as a result petitioner fell down from the motor cycle and sustainable grievous injury ?

with respect to the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.

To prove the accident and the accident was occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending Tata 709 Ex Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No.KA53AA1234, the petitioner himself got examined as PW1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.19.

The owner of the offendng vehicle has admitted the accident and also stated that one Taslimuddin was the driver of the offedning vehicle under reply to the police notice as per Ex.P.10.
14.
On the other hand, the respondent No.1 insurance company denied the rash and negligent SCCH-10 driving of the driver of the offending vehicle.

The respondent No.1 argued that, there is no damages to the offending vehicle, the petitioner himself fell down from the bike as self fall and sustained injury, the same is suggested to the PW1 and PW1 has denied it.
There is no documents to show the petitioner himself fell down from his bike.
The MLC as per Ex.P.6 discloses that the petitioner admitted on 11.10.2021 at about 11.30 p.m.,
Though there is a delay in filing the complaint, but MLC was registered on the same day.
Therefore, it cannot be doubt the case of the petition on delay in lodging the complaint.
Moreover, the owner has admitted the accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as accident occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

15. Therefore, on perusal of the records and evidence it shows that the accident was occurred on the sole negligence on the part of the driver of the offending SCCH-10 Tata 709 Ex Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA53AA1234.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate and discharge summaries as per Ex.P.16, Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15, it shows that, the petitioner sustained injury and taken treatment.
Hence, I answer the Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:
This petition is filed for seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the injuries sustained by the petitioner in the road traffic accident as stated above.

The specific contention of the petitioner that, he was riding his Two wheeler Dio bearing Reg. No.
KA02 JE0132 near Nirmala Medicals, Vijayanandanagar Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the TATA 709 EX Mini Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA 53AA1234 came with high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the petitioner's motor cycle from back side.
Due to the impact, the SCCH-10 petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident, he was shifted to Confident Hospital, Shankarnagar,
Bengaluru, wherein he has taken treatment as an inpatient, he was advised by the doctor to take rest and regular followup treatment.
Therefore, the petitioner become permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
17. In this case, the petitioner has proved the accident and injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident by producing cogent evidence.

Further the petitioner got examined Dr.Shekar.M as PW2 and got marked the documents i.e. Ex.P.20 is the OPD file, Ex.P.21 is the Case sheet and Ex.P.22 is the Xray.
18.
The PW2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner.

The doctor stated that, the petitioner has sustained injuries to his left leg i.e. a) Swelling left ankle with bleeding, b) Deformity left foot and c)
Lateral subtalar dislocation of left foot and under went surgery SCCH-10 of closed reduction and fixation with kwires for left foot and he was discharged on 16.10.2021 and he was again admitted Ramesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38174397/
5 on 13.12.2021 at the same hospital for another surgery to remove implants from left foot and was discharged on 14.12.201.
19.

sentences.text: Recently he examined the petitioner on 07.06.2023 and is of opinion that, a healed scar over medial side of left foot, tenderness present over the ankle and subtalar joints, the petitioner had restricted movements of left ankle and subtalar joints, he had moderate pain in left foot while walking and long standing and xray shows signs of subtalar arthritis.
Further PW2 doctor assessed the permanent disability of left lower limb at 42.76% and to whole body at 14,25%.
The PW2 is not the treated doctor.

So, in view of all these circumstances, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation under the following different heads:
SCCH-10 20. LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS ON THE ACCOUNT OF DISABILITY.

According to the petitioner he was working as Writer cum Clerk in Lakshmi Venkateshwar Traders,
Yeshwanthapura RMC Yard, Bengaluru and earning a salary of Rs.30,000/p.m.
To support of his claim with respect to avocation and earnings, he has not produced any documents.

However, he examined the Proprietor of Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara, Bengaluru as PW3 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.23 to Ex.P.26 i.e. Ex.P.23 is the Aadhaar card of PW3, Ex.P.24 is the License, Ex.P.25 is the Registration Certificate and Ex.P.26 is the Certificate u/s 65 B of Evidence Act.
The PW3 has admitted in his crossexamination that, he has maintained records for monthly payment of employees and he can produce it.
Further stated that he has not produced the document to show he has paid amount of Rs.1,000/ per day to the petitioner.
But the PW3 not produced any documents to show the petition is his SCCH-10 employee and he is paying Rs.30,000/ p.m. salary to the petitioner.

The counsel for the petitioner relied the decision reported in AIR 2018 SC 1347 between Jagdish Vs Mohan & Ors., in this decision the petitioner was the skilled carpenter and another decision reported in 2018 (4) AKR 538 between Anil Kumar Vs Branch Manager, National Ins. Co Ltd., wherein the petitioner was cleaner in the lorry.

In the present case,
though the petitioner examined the employer nothing has been produced and proved about the avocation and employment.
Hence, the decisions are not applicable to the present facts of the case.
In the absence of documentary proof it cannot be considered the oral evidence of PW3 as he was paying salary of Rs.30,000/ to the petitioner per month.

21. At this juncture, I would like to refer the SCCH-10 decision reported in 2023(4) KCCR 3603 (DB) between Aneesahemmed Vs Mohammed Yusuf and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, " C. Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 - Section 168 - Personal injuries - Determination of compensation - Claimant pleading that he was earning Rs.40,000/ from his transport business - But not producing any material to substantiate his claim Tribunal therefore taking income at Rs.6,000/ In terms of charge prepared by Legal Services Authority income taken at Rs.7,000/ per month - Disability taken as 40% and multiplier of 15 adopted by Tribunal maintained - Total compensation enhanced from Rs.8,46,200/ to Rs.9,23,200/."

22. So far as the age of petitioner is concerned, the petitioner contended that, at the time of accident,
he was aged about 38 years.
To prove the age, the petitioner has produced the notarized copies of Election ID, DL and Aadhaar card as per Ex.P.11 to Ex.P13 and it disclose the date of birth of the petitioner is 02.02.1980.
The accident has taken place on 11.10.2021.
Hence, it shows the age of the petitioner is 41 years at the time of accident.

Hence, the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is "14".
23.

The petitioner claims that, working as Writer cum Clerk in Sri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Traders,
Yeshwanthapura RMC Yard, Bengaluru and earning a SCCH-10 sum of Rs.30,000/p.m., and due to accidental injury he is unable to do work.
The petitioner also gave oral evidence and deposed before the Court that, he is unable to do his work as which he was doing earlier.
The petitioner got examined the doctor as PW2.
PW2 deposed in his affidavit chief evidence that the petitioner is suffering from the permanent disability of left lower limb as 42.76% and whole body disability at 14.25%.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied the decision of 2021 ACJ 753 between T.Elizabeth Vs M.Govindan & Another and another decision of 2021 ACJ 993 between Karthik Subramanian Vs B.Sarath Babu & Anr.
24.

sentences.text: The counsel for the respondent has cross examined the PW2 doctor and PW2 has stated that, "It is true that the petitioner has sustained injury to lower part of ankle and to the foot."

Further stated that;
" The petitioner not sustained fracture SCCH-10 but there is a dislocation of joint.
We fixed the dislocation of joint to the same place.
Alignment is normal, It is false to suggest that there is no necessity to surgery for fix the dislocation of joint.
It is false to suggest that the POP treatment is sufficient to the injury."

Further stated that;
"It is true that, we have fixed only Kwire treatment and the surgery was conducted on the same day of the accident."
Further stated that, "It is true that the injury of the petitioner is not open fracture and there is no infection at fracture site.
There is no loss of muscle strength and tendon.
Kwire was fixed only for temporary basis and it requires 6 to 8 weeks to remove the Kwire."

sentences.text: "It is true that the petitioner no need further treatment from the date of discharge till removal of kwires except medicine.
It is true that Kwire was removed within 2 months.
There is no complication in the injury SCCH-10 thereby kwire has been removed, witness says that is is part of the treatment thereby kwire was removed."
Further stated that, "It is true that usually we advise for physiotherapy and it is only exercise and the petitioner has to do exercise on his own.
It is false to suggest that the petitioner has not taken physiotherapy treatment."

On careful perusal of evidence of doctor it show that, according to the doctor's evidence the injuries are that a) Swelling left ankle with bleeding, b) Deformity left foot and c) Lateral subtalar dislocation of left foot.
According to the discharge summary as per Ex.P.14 the injuries diagnosed as Lateral subtalar dislocation of left foot.
The medical procedure for the such injury to the petitioner as per discharge summary is that closed reduction and internal fixation with Kwire.
Now the K wire was also removed as per discharge summary as per Ex.P.15.

Under these circumstances and considering the SCCH-10 injuries, treatment by the doctor and evidence of the PW 2, I am of the opinion that though the doctor has assessed the disability as 42.76% to the left lower limb and to the whole body is 14.25% is on higher side disability.
However, there an injury and treatment the disability as assessed by the doctor is only physical disability.
Hence, I am of the opinion that, the disability of the petitioner is to be taken as 10%.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for the compensation of Rs.2,52,000/ (Rs.15,000/ X 12 X 14 X 10/100) towards loss of future income on the account of disability of the petitioner.

25. PAIN AND SUFFERINGS:
As per the Wound certificate and Discharge summaries as per Ex.P.6, Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15, the petitioner has sustained injury to his left leg i.e. a) Swelling left ankle with bleeding, b) Deformity left foot and c) Lateral subtalar dislocation of left foot.

By SCCH-10 considering the above facts and discussion made above and looking to the nature of injuries, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.30,000/ under the head of Pain and sufferings.
26. LOSS OF AMENITIES
Further on perusal of evidence of PW1, it reveals that, petitioner has sustained grievous injuries.
The petitioner was aged about 38 years at the time of accident.

Considering the above facts and on perusal of evidence of PW1 and PW2, considering the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of amenities.
27. ATTENDANT, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
In this case has produced two discharge summaries as per Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15 of Confidence SCCH-10 Hospital, Bengaluru.
On perusal Ex.P.14 discharge summary, it shows that, the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient from 11.10.2021 to 16.10.2021 i.e., for a period of 6 days.

Further on perusal of another Discharge Ramesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38174397/
8 summary marked as per Ex.P.15, it shows that the petitioner has again taken inpatient treatment for a period of two days for removal of implant i.e. on 13.12.2021 to 14.12.2021.

The attendance and nourishment charges of the petitioner during the hospitalization is required.
Therefore it is proper to award the amount of Rs.8,000/ under the head of attendant, food and nourishment and conveyance charges.
28. LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD AND REST PERIOD:

Further due to the accidental injuries, the SCCH-10 petitioner might have taken rest at least for a period of one month as per evidence of doctor PW2 he has sustained injuries to his left leg i.e. a) Swelling left ankle with bleeding, b) Deformity left foot and c) Lateral subtalar dislocation of left foot and as such, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs. 15,000/ under the head of loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
29. MEDICAL EXPENSES

As regard to claim of medical expenses, the petitioner has produced Medical bills as per Ex.P.16 along with medical prescriptions as per Ex.P.17, contending that he has made total expenses to the tune of Rs.2,14,309/.
The respondents has not disputed the said medical bills.
Therefore, by considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, I proceed to award Rs.2,14,309/ under the head of medical expenses.

sentences.text: Further, as stated above that, the alleged accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and admittedly the policy was in force as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner because already it is held under Issue No.1 as the accident has occurred on the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.5,39,309/ with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit.

Accordingly,
I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.

32. ISSUE No.3: In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
SCCH-10 O R D E R The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,39,309/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, in view of the valid policy, the respondent No.1/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.

After deposit of compensation amount, 30% amount with interest shall be kept in FD SCCH-10 in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/ schedule bank of his choice for the period of 3 years and remaining amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
:
The petitioner has filed this claim petition against the respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ with interest for the injuries sustained by him in a Road Traffic Accident took place on 11.10.2021.
2.
The respondent No.1 being insurer and the respondent No.2 being owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Ramesh.A vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/38174397/
2 petitioner.
Further it has admitted for the issuance of insurance policy in respect of the offending vehicle and in favour of the respondent No.2.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Further SCCH-10 contended that, the owner of the offending vehicle willfully entrusted the vehicle to the person who did not possess a valid and effective DL as on the date of accident and seeks protection u/s 147 and 149 of M.V. Act.
7.
It is the allegation of the respondent No.1 that neither the owner nor jurisdictional police complied the mandatory provisions as required u/s 134(c) and 158(6) of Motor Vehicles Act.
It is the specific contention of this respondent that, the petitioner himself solely responsible for the cause of alleged accident.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is excessive and exorbitant.
Hence,
prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
The counsel for the petitioner relied the decision reported in AIR 2018 SC 1347 between Jagdish Vs Mohan & Ors., in this decision the petitioner was the skilled carpenter and another decision reported in 2018 (4) AKR 538 between Anil Kumar Vs Branch Manager, National Ins. Co Ltd., wherein the petitioner was cleaner in the lorry.
PW2 deposed in his affidavit chief evidence that the petitioner is suffering from the permanent disability of left lower limb as 42.76% and whole body disability at 14.25%.
The counsel for the petitioner has relied the decision of 2021 ACJ 753 between T.Elizabeth Vs M.Govindan & Another and another decision of 2021 ACJ 993 between Karthik Subramanian Vs B.Sarath Babu & Anr.
24.
opennyai_summary.issue:
8. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed :
ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 11.10.2021 at about 10.55 a.m., while the petitioner was proceeding on his Two Wheeler Dio bearing Reg. No.KA02JE0132 and when he reached near Nirmala Medicals, Vijayanagar SCCH-10 Road, Nandini Layout, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of the Tata 709 Ex Mini Lorry bearing No.KA53AA1234 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner with a high speed and dashed to the petitioner's motor cycle from behind, as a result petitioner fell down from the motor cycle and sustainable grievous injury ?

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
13. After the accident, one Venkatesh, relative of the petitioner, lodged the complaint against the driver of the Tata 709 EX Mini Lorry bearing Reg. No. KA53AA SCCH-10 1234 and FIR was registered against the driver of offending vehicle for the offence punishable U/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC.
The FIR and complaint are produced as per Ex.P.1 and Ex.P.2 and after investigation the police have filed charge sheet as per Ex.P.9 against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offence punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC as the accident had occurred due to rash and negligent driving of driver of offending vehicle.
Moreover, the owner has admitted the accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle as accident occurred on the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The petitioner has produced the wound certificate and discharge summaries as per Ex.P.16, Ex.P.14 and Ex.P.15, it shows that, the petitioner sustained injury and taken treatment.
Due to the impact, the SCCH-10 petitioner fell down on the road and sustained grievous injuries.
Therefore, the petitioner become permanently disabled and lost his earning capacity.
17. In this case, the petitioner has proved the accident and injuries sustained by him in the alleged accident by producing cogent evidence.
The PW2 has assessed the disability of the petitioner.
In the present case,
though the petitioner examined the employer nothing has been produced and proved about the avocation and employment.
In the absence of documentary proof it cannot be considered the oral evidence of PW3 as he was paying salary of Rs.30,000/ to the petitioner per month.
Therefore in view of the above decision and in the absence of proof of income the income has to be taken SCCH-10 into consideration as per the Charge prepared by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority, Bengaluru.
The accident was occurred on 11.10.2021.
Therefore, Rs.15,000/ has to be taken into consideration as monthly income of the petitioner.
The accident has taken place on 11.10.2021.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Therefore, by considering the above bills and injuries sustained by the petitioner in the accident, I proceed to award Rs.2,14,309/ under the head of medical expenses.
SCCH-10 30
. By considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reasons, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.5,39,309/ under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation  amount 1. Towards loss of future earning Rs. 2,52,000/ capacity due to permanent disability 2.
Towards Pain and Sufferings Rs. 30,000/
3. Towards loss of Amenities Rs. 20,000/
4.Towards attendant, food and Rs. 8,000/ nourishment and conveyance charges 5.
Towards loss of income during Rs. 15,000/ laid up period and rest period.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 and 2 being owner and insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner because already it is held under Issue No.1 as the accident has occurred on the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
However, the respondent No.1 being the insurer of offending vehicle is liable to pay compensation of Rs.5,39,309/ with interest @ 6% p.a., from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly,
I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
32. ISSUE No.3: In view of my finding on issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following;
SCCH-10 O R D E R The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.5,39,309/ with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, in view of the valid policy, the respondent No.1/insurance company is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner and directed to deposit the compensation amount in this tribunal within two months from the date of this order.
After deposit of compensation amount, 30% amount with interest shall be kept in FD SCCH-10 in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/ schedule bank of his choice for the period of 3 years and remaining amount with accrued interest shall be released to the petitioner through NEFT/RTGS by way of Epayment on proper identification.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
